resources.string: Runs per-platform tasks and switches apps when each is done

Only after you enable it and start a task, the service switches apps through your queue and swipes up. With content targeting on, it reads the accessible text of the current target video page and decides locally whether to stay or skip. Reading text for comments always needs an explicit request from the notification.

Video Browse Assistant watches window changes and performs swipes. Content targeting, once you turn it on, reads the accessible text of the current target video page and filters it on this device by your wanted/unwanted topics. It never uploads page content, never reads accounts or messages and never posts comments by itself.

Android shows one foreground app at a time, so the assistant switches apps in queue order. It only browses videos in the foreground, swipes and counts progress; content targeting and comment assistance are separate opt-ins. It never interacts, reads messages or solves captchas for you.
Each area has its own page; the overview keeps only status, statistics and the start button.

The service is on. Pick platforms under Tasks to run them in order with automatic switching.

Android opens the main Accessibility page. Scroll to Downloaded apps or Installed services, choose Video Browse Assistant accessibility service and turn it on, then come back and check that the status says On. If the service is missing or its switch is greyed out, open app info and look for Allow restricted settings in the top-right menu.

Domestic and international platforms can share one batch. Pick platforms first, then set the number of videos for each.
Each video waits a random 10–30 seconds before the swipe; the interval is never fixed.
Platforms run in the order you picked them and switch when their quota is reached. Some apps need their video feed opened once beforehand.

Choose topics you want and do not want. The assistant reads only the accessible text of the current video page and decides on this device: matches stay for the usual interval, others are skipped early. It does not change the app\'s recommendations and never uploads page content.
Use content targeting (from the next session)
For example: AI, product reviews, study plans

When on, the assistant reads the accessible text of the target video page only while a session you started is in the foreground, and decides on this device whether to stay or skip. Page text is never uploaded or written to diagnostics, and nothing is liked, commented or changed in the app\'s recommendations. Each session freezes your topics and scan limit, and its data is cleared when it stops.
Content targeting is off; browsing uses the random 10–30 second rhythm.

On the video page, tap Pause and read in the notification, then come back to generate suggestions. If no text can be read, add the key points yourself. Suggestions come from this device or your configured model gateway and are never posted automatically.

Only when you tap Pause and read in the notification on a target video does the assistant read the page\'s accessible text to suggest comments. The text is cleared when you resume, stop, or after 5 minutes. Without the model gateway nothing goes online; accounts and messages are never read and nothing is posted automatically.

Provider keys stay on the server. Only when you pause a video and tap Generate does this app send the minimum page text, keywords and tone to your HTTPS gateway; accounts and messages are never sent and nothing is posted automatically.

Only after you pause on a video page and tap Generate will this app send up to 360 characters of accessible page text, your keywords and tone to the HTTPS gateway you configured. The device token stays in memory for this app session only, and model/API keys can never be entered here. The gateway never posts comments; you always send them yourself.
